name: Carney Complex-Trismus-Pseudocamptodactyly Syndrome
aliases: Carney Complex with Trismus and Pseudocamptodactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Carney Complex Diagnostic Criteria (modified for trismus-pseudocamptodactyly variant)

criteria.description: Presence of cardiac myxomas confirmed by imaging or histology
Clinical evidence of trismus combined with pseudocamptodactyly
Spotty skin pigmentation including lentigines or blue nevi
Presence of endocrine tumors such as pituitary adenomas or adrenal hyperplasia
Positive family history of Carney complex or related features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both cardiac myxoma and trismus-pseudocamptodactyly or one major criterion plus two minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including cardiology, genetics, and orthopedics.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe limitation of jaw opening due to fibrosis or muscle contracture

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pseudocamptodactyly characterized by finger flexion deformity on wrist extension
pathognomonic.notes: Dynamic finger deformity triggered by wrist movement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cardiac myxomas causing intracardiac obstruction or embolic events

common.symptomName: Spotty skin pigmentation including lentigines and blue nevi
common.notes: Typically on face, lips, and conjunctiva

common.symptomName: Endocrine abnormalities such as Cushing syndrome or acromegaly
common.notes: Due to pituitary or adrenal involvement
Benign skin tumors often on trunk and limbs

common.symptomName: Muscle contractures beyond trismus affecting limb joints
common.notes: May contribute to limited range of motion
searchTerms: muscle tightness affecting arms and legs

occasional.notes: May lead to growth hormone excess or prolactin abnormalities
Includes atrial fibrillation or conduction blocks
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to myxomas

occasional.symptomName: Oropharyngeal myxomas contributing to airway obstruction
Depression or anxiety related to chronic disease burden
searchTerms: mental health issues with chronic disease

rare.symptomName: Adrenal hyperplasia leading to primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease
Stroke or embolic events due to cardiac myxoma fragments
searchTerms: brain embolism due to cardiac myxoma
blood clots from heart tumor causing stroke

laboratory: Elevated cortisol levels in cases with adrenal involvement
imaging: MRI of pituitary gland showing adenomas
CT or MRI of jaw muscles showing fibrosis or contracture
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern consistent with autosomal dominant transmission
other: Histopathology confirming myxoma in cardiac or cutaneous lesions
Clinical observation of pseudocamptodactyly during wrist movement

distinguishingFeatures: Similar skin pigmentation and myxomas but different musculoskeletal involvement
Progressive heterotopic ossification rather than myxomas
Congenital malformations of the great toes absent in Carney complex-trismus-pseudocamptodactyly syndrome
Endocrine tumors without cardiac myxomas or pseudocamptodactyly

redFlags: Sudden onset of neurological deficits indicating embolic stroke
Rapidly enlarging cardiac mass causing heart failure symptoms
Severe trismus impairing airway management or nutrition
references: Carney JA. The complex of myxomas, spotty pigmentation, and endocrine overactivity. Medicine (Baltimore). 1985;64(4):270-283.
Stratakis CA. Carney complex: clinical and molecular features. Front Horm Res. 2013;41:50-64.
